overview: Agents push batches to collectors which write to Kafka; consumers write to a sharded TSDB; a Flink job computes 1-min/1-h rollups; alert evaluator reads recent data from Kafka/stream and notifies via PagerDuty.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative fleet: 10K hosts × 1K series, scraped every 15 s.
estimation.result: 15 days at 16 raw bytes/sample ≈ 13.8 TB before compression/replication.
estimation.implication: Control label cardinality; downsample historical blocks and separate ingestion from expensive queries.

steps.title: Host agents → LB → Collectors → Metrics stream → TSDB writers → TSDB
steps.explanation: Validate label cardinality, append durably and batch-write raw samples.

steps.title: Metrics stream → Rollups → TSDB
steps.explanation: Compute time-window rollups and retain older data at lower resolution.

steps.title: Dashboards → LB → Query Service → TSDB
steps.explanation: Bound time range, resolution and series count for dashboard queries.

steps.title: Rollups → Alert evaluator → Notifier → PagerDuty
steps.explanation: Evaluate sustained threshold conditions and deduplicate pages.

failureCases.scenario: A target disappears or ingestion backs up
failureCases.handling: Track scrape failures and missing series separately from zero values. Alert on collection health, cap buffers, and expose dropped-sample counters rather than hiding data gaps.

alternatives: Use push collectors and a replayable stream for high ingest rates and short-lived producers. Use pull scraping with local WAL/TSDB for discoverable long-lived targets, adding object blocks and HA query deduplication for global retention.
